name: closeness_centrality
author: 7065a2b5
description: Ranks nodes by closeness centrality: how short their shortest-path distances to all other nodes are (inverse average distance, with the Wasserman-Faust correction for disconnected graphs). Use it for questions like 'who can reach everyone fastest?', 'which airport is most central / closest to all others?' or 'how central is X?' (pass node). Works on directed and undirected graphs, weighted or not. Distances are hop counts by default; set weighted=true to use edge weights (e.g. km). On directed graphs, direction='incoming' (default, as NetworkX) measures distance from the others to each node; use 'outgoing' for distance from each node to the others ('who can reach everyone'). Returns the top_k nodes with score (higher = more central), or for one node its score, rank, average distance and number of nodes reached.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

top_k.description: How many of the most central nodes to return.

node.description: Optional node id: return only this node's closeness and rank. Use lookup_node to find the id from a name.

weighted.description: true: use edge weights as distances (Dijkstra). false: count hops (breadth-first search).

direction.description: Directed graphs only. 'incoming': distance from the other nodes to this node. 'outgoing': distance from this node to the others. Ignored on undirected graphs.
